caveat: Rig input is synthetic, not a finger: Android injects at 120 Hz through a uinput touchscreen and desktop through CDP, each through the browser's real input pipeline; iOS input is HID through idb on a leased simulator, which delivers a move every ~30 ms (not 120 Hz), so iOS speeds are the distance Safari delivered between the first and last moving pointermove, over that time. A physical finger's 120–240 Hz jittered sampling is not reproduced.

injected.source: idb ui swipe (companion-side steps of 60 pt), iOS 26.2 simulator, iPhone 17 Pro; the companion delivers a step about every 30 ms (measured), not at a set rate
injected.speedFrom: Safari's delivery: the first to the last moving pointermove

release.note: idb lifts 58 ms after the last move, longer than the 40 ms stillness interval, which a finger lifting mid-motion does not do: the replay releases at the last move. The simulator delivers each step 29-44 ms apart (six samples here): against the speed Safari delivered, from its first to its last moving pointermove, the pan release reads 7.2% under and the scroll release 12.2% under. One misses 10%, so this fling is not velocity evidence, and only its direction and axis are checked
